body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 8cd4c91887ea361302dd6438ea00e6e745726a9b -->
**Needs changes before merge.** Two small fixes. The geometry is safe, but the comments name the wrong layer as the containment guarantee, and the macOS bore pin should take the value measured below. This review was asked for while the PR is still a draft. The draft state is left as it is.

### What looks good
- The containment argument holds. Douglas-Peucker keeps every dropped vertex within `tol` of its chord, so the thinned boundary is within 0.25 um of the original (Hausdorff), and the straight-line homotopy between them stays inside that tube. Eroding by `rho + INSET`, with `INSET = SIMPLIFY + ARC_TOL + 10 nm`, therefore only keeps points more than `rho + 0.26 um` inside the original area. Dilating by `rho` cannot reach a wall or an island. The intersection with `r` comes on top of that. The final lap ends up about 0.5 um farther off the wall than before, which only leaves stock.
- The loop/hole-count fallback rejects obvious topology changes. Containment does not depend on it (see the mutation results).
- No budget, load, travel, crossing or final-path guard is touched. The only test edit is the Linux bore triple.
- Ring nesting is no longer *proved*, and the grow.rs header now says so. The per-ring perturbation (< 1 um) is well under `GAP` (2.5 um), and a crossing would still be refused by `guard.rs` and fall back by name rather than post.
- Process: the body is complete (what changed, how tested, limitations, `Changelog:`, `Fixes #882`). Commit subjects are conventional. `docs/decisions/882-adaptive-open-simplify.md` is present. Provenance lines are on `simplify.rs` and both new test files. Every file stays under 400 lines (grow.rs 382). No snapshot PNGs or goldens. `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` appear only in tests. No other CAM product is named.
- The `chore(process): sync` commits are noise only. The net diff against `main` has no process file, and `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is 52 on both sides, so "process version 52" in the body is accurate.

### Local results (macOS arm64, merged with main `ee05ba8`, clean merge)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | ok, 1.0 min. motion lib 272 passed / 5 ignored. adaptive_band 2, adaptive_hsm 1 (+5 ignored), adaptive_orbit_seam 1, motion pocket3d_hsm 3 (+1), app pocket3d_hsm 1 (+1) |
| motion heavy lanes, release `--ignored adaptive` (lib) | 5/5 ok, 33.5 s, including budget fixtures, twins and slot perturbations |
| motion `adaptive_hsm` + `pocket3d_hsm`, release `--include-ignored` | 6/6 and 4/4 ok |
| app `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore...`, release | every safety assert passes (no warnings, no fallback, no budget note). **Fails the macOS exact triple only**, see below. 2.3 s (main: 123.6 s on this machine) |
| clippy `-p camcraft-motion --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |
| clippy `-p camcraft-app --lib --test pocket3d_hsm -D warnings` | clean. `--all-targets` stops on `tests/wire_stamp.rs` (missing `taper_deg`), which is broken on `main` itself (#1377), not here |

STEP bore on macOS arm64, release, two runs identical:
```
PR head   : moves 16026 planar 15382 arcs 1413   (Z 20: 49 microlift returns, 9 rides, 1 retract hop)
main      : moves 16070 planar 15357 arcs 1486
pinned    : (16160, 15432, 1571)   -- already stale on main before this PR
```

### Mutation checks (motion lib `simplify` tests, plus all motion adaptive suites for A+B)
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| A: drop `.intersect(r)` in `open` | **survives**, all tests pass |
| B: drop the loop/hole-count fallback (`Some(out)`) | **survives** |
| A+B together, across lib + adaptive_band/hsm/orbit_seam/pocket3d_hsm | **survives**, all pass |
| C: drop the intersection and set `INSET = 0` | caught: 3 tests fail (`0.2 um wall by hole, R0.08: opening adds 0.00105 mm2 outside its source`) |
| D: keep the intersection, set `INSET = 0` | caught: 3 tests fail (lattice slivers, `cyclic seam, R0.6: opening adds 2.8e-8 mm2`, `rho 0.6: boundary samples outside the area opened left: 2748`) |

So `INSET` is what keeps the opened area inside the original, and the tests pin it. The intersection alone does not pass the PR's own containment tests (D), and removing it changes nothing any test sees (A).

### Requested before merge
1. **Name the guarantee correctly and pin it.** `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/rings.rs:49-51` ("The exact region intersection is the containment backstop"), `rings.rs:44-46` ("it is not a topology proof"), `simplify.rs:20-23` and the decision record say the intersection is the backstop. The measurements say the opposite: the erosion margin `INSET > SIMPLIFY + ARC_TOL` is the guarantee, and the intersection is defence in depth. Please reword those comments, and add a one-line assertion test (for example `assert!(INSET > SIMPLIFY + ARC_TOL)`) so a later "tidy" cannot shrink the margin on the strength of a comment that says the clip already covers it. Keeping the intersection is fine.
2. **Update the macOS arm of the bore pin.** At `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:133`, change `(16160, 15432, 1571)` to `(16026, 15382, 1413)`, measured at this head on Apple silicon in release (two runs, identical; every level verifies clean, none falls back). Main itself measures `(16070, 15357, 1486)` here, so that arm was already stale. Windows stays owed.

### Notes (not blocking)
- Mutation B surviving is expected: by the argument above, containment holds without the count check. It is worth saying in `within`'s doc that the check is there to keep the topology, not containment.
- The planner is about 50x faster on the bore here (123.6 s to 2.3 s, release), which matches the PR's Linux numbers.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
